lines.cap: Late winter. A stag's antlers simply fall off. Both of them, within days.
lines.say: Late winter. A stag's antlers simply fall off. Both of them, within days.

lines.cap: Then they grow back, from scratch. Up to two and a half centimetres a day.
lines.say: Then they grow back, from scratch. Up to two and a half centimetres a day.

lines.cap: That's some of the fastest growing tissue of any mammal.

lines.cap: While they grow, they're covered in soft, fuzzy skin called velvet, full of blood vessels.

lines.cap: By late summer they harden into bone, and he rubs the velvet off on trees.

lines.cap: Then it's autumn, and he uses them to fight other males, and impress the females.

lines.cap: As he gets older and stronger, the rack usually gets bigger.
